findings.text: When dummy.stack has no newline (e.g., "Error"), firstNewlineIndex is -1 and the code returns empty string instead of preserving the original stack, losing error information.

When stack has fewer than two newlines (e.g., "at foo\nat bar"), secondNewlineIndex is -1 and stackWithoutTwoTopLines becomes empty string; since every string ends with empty string, the condition fails and the stack is never appended even when err.stack doesn't contain it.

0.reason: This describes the same root cause as the reference bug: when the stack lacks a newline, the code returns an empty string, losing error information, which is the same mechanism of mishandling missing newlines in the reconstructed stack.

1.reason: This directly matches the reference bug: when the reconstructed stack has fewer than two newlines, stackWithoutTwoTopLines becomes empty and endsWith('') is always true, so the stack is never appended.
